paragraph: Old Tappan is a single-family town first, with 21 sales over six months at a median of $1,460,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00. Slightly under half sold above asking and the median sat 28 days on market, which reads competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with three full baths, and prices ran from $689,000 to $2,850,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Monthly medians built through spring to a June peak around $1,736,250 before easing in July, which is exactly the normal Bergen arc, and with four to seven closings in the busier months there isn't enough volume to read much more into it than that. Townhouses are the smaller tier, seven sales at a median of $870,000, moving faster at 14 days with a ratio slightly above list. Most are three-bedroom townhouses with three baths. If you're comparing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
